newsitem.title: UK: Major calls new IRA attack "sickening hypocrisy".
newsitem.headline: Major calls new IRA attack "sickening hypocrisy".

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Tuesday that the IRA's admission that it carried out Monday's bombing of British Army headquarters in Northern Ireland was "sickening hypocrisy".

He told reporters at the Conservative Party's last annual conference before the next election that Gerry Adams, leader of the political wing of the Irish Republican Army (IRA), had shown his true colours.
"So much of what Mr Adams...and the IRA have said in the last two years is nothing less than sickening hypocrisy," he said.

"Within the last few days Mr Adams has been asking to come and talk to me, asking to carry the peace process forward and all the time he knew they had planned to murder people in Lisburn. I hope people will see very clearly precisely what they are and treat their words for what they are worth."
Thirty-one people, including 20 soldiers, were injured in the twin car bombs on Monday afternoon within the perimeters of army headquarters in Lisburn, near Belfast.

It was the first attack in the province by the IRA, which has waged a 25-year battle against British rule in Northern Ireland, since it broke a 17-month ceasefire in February, and the most serious setback to the struggling peace process since it began in 1993.
